clue.text: Chopped meat is sent to cafés

definitions.note: plural noun matching a plural answer: small French bars or bistros

indicators.note: chopped meat is cut up, so the letters of the following words are cut up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Minced meat being delivered to some little restaurants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chopped' looks like it describes the meat but signals that MEAT IS SENT is rearranged; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An estaminet is a small French bar or bistro, a cheap café-restaurant.

clue.text: Island where Nellie lost her head

indicators.note: losing the head means the first letter of the singer's surname is dropped

parts.note: Nellie Melba was the famous Australian opera soprano, known by that stage name

explanation.surface: A place where some woman called Nellie was beheaded.
explanation.walkthrough: Nellie is not a stray first name: it points to Dame Nellie Melba, whose surname without its first letter is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Elba is the Mediterranean island where Napoleon was exiled in 1814.

clue.text: They work on land, and at sea

definitions.text: They work on land, and at sea

parts.words: They work on land, and at sea
parts.note: farmers who till the soil work on land, while the bars that steer a boat's rudder work at sea: one word covers both

explanation.surface: Some workers busy both ashore and afloat.
explanation.definitionFit: Tillers are people who cultivate soil, and also the levers used to turn a boat's rudder.

clue.text: Fairly joyful revolutionary

parts.note: something found at a fair, cheerful, and spinning round and round: a fairground ride, not a political rebel

explanation.surface: A rebel who is only moderately happy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fairly' seems to mean 'quite', but it means 'at a fair'; 'revolutionary' is literal rotation.
explanation.definitionFit: A carousel is a fairground ride that turns in circles, with a jolly mood.

clue.text: Game pie cooked in northern hostelries

indicators.note: in places the cooked letters inside the word for hostelries

parts.note: hostelries are inns

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters of the following word are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: A game pie prepared in pubs in the north of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' looks like an adjective describing the pie, but it is the definition; 'cooked' is the anagram signal and 'in' the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninepins is the old bowling game of knocking down nine wooden pins.

clue.text: It's no great shakes

parts.note: the idiom for something unimpressive is read literally: a small, slight shaking movement

explanation.surface: Something that is decidedly unremarkable.
explanation.definitionFit: A tremor is a slight quiver or minor earthquake, literally a shake that is not great.

clue.text: A song among the proletariat

indicators.note: among says the letters are found within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A tune that is popular with working-class people.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is a solo song, especially in an opera.

clue.text: A relict might give such a performance

indicators.note: the letters of the words before might give, once rearranged, a new word

explanation.surface: A widow perhaps putting on a show.
explanation.walkthrough: A relict is an old word for a widow. 'might give' signals rearranging A RELICT; 'such a' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a musical or poetry performance by a soloist or small group.

clue.text: So it's a case of their getting together

definitions.text: So it's a case of their getting together

indicators.note: getting together suggests the letters of the phrase are assembled anew in another order

explanation.surface: An explanation that companions are those who gather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting together' rearranges SO IT'S A CASE; the whole clue also describes partners who come together.
explanation.definitionFit: Associates are companions or partners, people who join with one another.

clue.text: A musician at your door

parts.note: a player of church bells, or else the visitor who presses the button by the front door

explanation.surface: A street performer on the doorstep.
explanation.definitionFit: A campanologist rings church bells; anyone pressing a doorbell also rings one.

clue.text: Experts make threats to dismiss men

indicators.note: dismissing the men means removing those letters from the word for making threats

parts.note: to make threats is to menace, here in the form menaces
taken as written

explanation.surface: Specialists intimidate people to get workers sacked.
explanation.definitionFit: Aces are people who excel at something, top performers.

clue.text: One of Harry Feversham's four Masonic emblems

definitions.text: One of Harry Feversham's four Masonic emblems

parts.words: One of Harry Feversham's four Masonic emblems
parts.note: the hero of A. E. W. Mason's novel The Four Feathers receives four tokens of cowardice; 'Masonic' means from Mason's book

explanation.surface: A symbol of Freemasonry owned by a man named Harry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Masonic' suggests Freemasons, but means belonging to the novelist A. E. W. Mason.
explanation.definitionFit: In The Four Feathers, Feversham is sent white feathers, traditional tokens branding someone a coward.

clue.text: Identical in a high degree

definitions.meaning: as in 'the ... same', meaning exactly that one
an adverb meaning extremely or greatly

explanation.surface: Something that is exactly the same to a great extent.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means precisely the same (that very spot) and, as an adverb, extremely.

clue.text: "O my —— soul! My uncle!" (Hamlet)

parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from Hamlet, said when the Ghost confirms his suspicion of his uncle

explanation.surface: A line from Hamlet with one word missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet calls his soul foreseeing because it had already suspected Claudius of the murder.

clue.text: His job pays well, they say

definitions.text: His job pays well, they say

parts.words: His job pays well, they say
parts.note: the slogan 'it pays to advertise' is behind this: the man whose work is publicity

explanation.surface: A well-paid occupation, according to rumour.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying 'it pays to advertise' suggests that someone who promotes goods in publicity profits.

clue.text: It's a bit off !

parts.note: the complaint 'that's rather unfair' read literally as a small amount taken off a price

explanation.surface: A complaint that something is not quite fair.
explanation.definitionFit: A discount is a reduction, a small sum taken off the price.

clue.text: She can set all in a whirl

indicators.note: in a whirl means spun around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman who can throw everyone into confusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' is linking; 'in a whirl' rearranges SET ALL into a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Stella is a girl's name, so it stands for a woman.

clue.text: Jewelry items finish in bags

indicators.note: in puts the finish inside the bags

parts.note: bags is slang for loose trousers, pants
a finish is an end

explanation.surface: Jewellery ends up in handbags.
explanation.definitionFit: Pendants are ornaments hanging from a chain around the neck.

clue.text: Wrong-doer captures Italian pressman

indicators.note: captures says the jumbled letters enclose the abbreviation for Italian
wrong signals the word after it is set out in a wrong order

parts.note: taken as written
IT is a common abbreviation for Italian, as in Italian vermouth

explanation.surface: A criminal kidnaps an Italian journalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrong-doer' reads as one word meaning criminal, but splits: 'Wrong' is the anagram signal acting on the second half alone.
explanation.definitionFit: An editor is a newspaper man, a member of the press in charge of copy.

clue.text: No sense in it, any form it takes

indicators.note: any form it takes means the letters may be formed into another order

explanation.surface: Something is meaningless however you look at it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' rearranges IN IT ANY; 'it takes' is the surface's filler around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Inanity is silliness or emptiness, a lack of meaning.

clue.text: This man's creation being a DIY job?

definitions.text: This man's creation being a DIY job?

parts.words: This man's creation being a DIY job?
parts.note: someone who made his own way in life is jokingly described as having built himself, like home improvement

explanation.surface: A man who seems to have built himself at home.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-made person rose to success by their own efforts, as if built by themselves.

clue.text: Land of 6 inhabited by men

indicators.note: inhabited by means men live inside the answer to 6

parts.note: refers to the answer to 6 Across, a song
taken as written

explanation.surface: A country populated by men, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: Armenia is a country in the Caucasus.

clue.text: Doone at head of the board

definitions.meaning: ... Doone is the villain of R. D. Blackmore's novel Lorna Doone
the person who sits at the top of the dining table and cuts the joint

explanation.surface: A member of the Doone clan chairing a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'board' looks like a company board but is the old sense of a dining table.
explanation.definitionFit: Carver Doone is the novel's outlaw; one who slices the meat sits at the table's head.

clue.text: John Gilpin's men were not itinerant players

definitions.text: John Gilpin's men were not itinerant players

parts.words: John Gilpin's men were not itinerant players
parts.note: Cowper's John Gilpin was a captain of a citizen militia; the term also sounds like musicians on a railway journey

explanation.surface: The followers of John Gilpin did not perform on tour.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cowper's comic ballad, Gilpin was 'a train-band captain eke was he': a London militia company. Read literally, it might be a band touring by rail.
explanation.definitionFit: A train band was a company of citizen soldiers in London from the 16th to 18th centuries.

clue.text: Members taken up with conflicting views

definitions.meaning: weapons, which are taken up by those in conflict

explanation.surface: Club members adopted with differing opinions.
explanation.definitionFit: Arms are limbs of the body, and weapons are what people take up to fight.

clue.text: Lost by Ben Battle before he laid down his 24

definitions.text: Lost by Ben Battle before he laid down his 24

parts.words: Lost by Ben Battle before he laid down his 24
parts.note: in Thomas Hood's comic poem Faithful Nelly Gray, a cannonball took off the soldier's limbs, so he laid down his weapons, the answer to 24

explanation.surface: Something a soldier lost before surrendering his weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: Hood's lines: 'a cannon-ball took off his legs, so he laid down his arms', punning on surrendering.
explanation.definitionFit: Hood's soldier Ben Battle lost his lower limbs to a cannonball.

clue.text: It revolutionized cooking, and some waiters' pay

definitions.text: It revolutionized cooking, and some waiters' pay

parts.words: It revolutionized cooking, and some waiters' pay
parts.note: a rotating skewer turns meat while it roasts, and the gratuities waiters receive, turned round, give the same word

explanation.surface: An invention that transformed cookery and restaurant wages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionized' seems to mean transformed, but means turned round: the roasting rod revolves, and TIPS read backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A spit is a rotating rod for roasting meat over a fire.

clue.text: Opportunity coming late in the day — no odds

definitions.text: Opportunity coming late in the day
definitions.meaning: a chance that comes at eventide, in the evening
a fifty-fifty prospect, where no odds are offered

explanation.surface: A chance arriving late, with no betting odds.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a fifty-fifty probability; 'even' is also poetic for evening, plus opportunity.

clue.text: Straight from lighthouses to Billingsgate?

definitions.meaning: the straight beams of light shining out from lighthouses
flat fish sold at Billingsgate, London's fish market; the question mark marks an example

explanation.surface: Something coming directly from lighthouses to a fish market.
explanation.walkthrough: Billingsgate is London's wholesale fish market; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Rays are beams of light and also flat cartilaginous fish such as skate.

clue.text: No clean job working at this programme?

definitions.text: No clean job working at this programme?

parts.words: No clean job working at this programme?
parts.note: a dirty job is a cross one, and road works happen at a junction; the programme is a long-running television soap opera

explanation.surface: A messy job on a television show.
explanation.walkthrough: Crossroads was a long-running British TV soap opera set in a motel, from 1964.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossroads is where two roads intersect; Crossroads was also a British TV soap opera.
